source_text: Video aliam legem in membris meis, repugnantem legi mentis meae sed describebat humanam in hac corruptibili carne naturam, non opere Dei cum vitio primitus institutam, sed ex voluntatis arbitrio veniente primorum hominum vitio sauciatam.
pass_a_gloss: Sees aliam law in members meis, repugnantem legi of-the-mind my but describebat humanam in hac corruptibili in-flesh nature, not by-work of-God when/with by-vice primitus institutam, but from of-will by-decision veniente primorum of-human-beings by-vice sauciatam.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium

pass_b_english: The apostle was portraying a Jewish person living under the law when he said: “I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh” (Romans 7:18); “It is not I who do it, but sin that dwells in me” (Romans 7:17); “Evil lies close beside me” (Romans 7:21); and “I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind” (Romans 7:23).

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
